title: connectFakeClient is re-declared in 88 test files and the connection-store reset has four drifted spellings
note: Counts re-measured: 89 files define connectFakeClient, 456 connectionStore.setState calls; idle-reset spellings: 182 {state,serverInfo,client}, 25 with features, 12 {state,client}, 7 {state,client,serverInfo}, plus singletons, so drift is real and connection.ts has no reset-for-tests (many sibling stores do: resetAgentsDocStoreForTests etc.). It is boilerplate and a minor leak risk, not an actively bug-causing defect, so medium. Fix-plan caution: connectionStore.setState is a wrapped setter (connection.ts:58-84) so a reset helper should be built on it; resetting in the global per-test hook in testSetup.ts could break files that connect in beforeAll or module scope, so do it as an opt-in helper first and a global hook only after a CI run.
revised_fix_plan: Add resetConnectionStoreForTests() in stores/connection.ts (matching the other stores' convention) and a shared connectReadyFakeClient in a src/testing module; codemod files in batches, replacing the setState spellings with the helper. Only then consider a testSetup.ts global reset, validated on CI. Document in testing.md.

title: Thread, capabilities and read-response fixtures are re-declared in ~85 files although appwire-client/testing already has wireThread
note: Verified: 85 files contain changeVisionModel: true across src/appwire/mobile; 36 declare 'const CAPABILITIES: ThreadCapabilities'; 27 define testThread and 27 define readResponse; wireThread imported by only 4 web files. notifications.ts:1-3 states the write-once intent; notifications.ts:13 and tokenFlood.ts:243 each hold their own CAPABILITIES copy (note notifications.ts' copy is untyped, tokenFlood's is typed ThreadCapabilities). mobile-native/src/dev/demoSessions.ts is a dev demo, not a test fixture, so exclude it from the migration or treat it separately. Fixtures drift in small ways, so the per-family override approach is right.

title: Async and jsdom-environment helpers are reinvented per file beside existing shared ones
note: Core right but overcounted in places. Real local deferred definitions: 16 files (function/const form; the grep 'own deferred' count of 18 includes AppShell.test.tsx local variables named deferred). Some local copies drop reject (needsYouActions.test.ts:43), so they are subsets of the shared helper and safe to swap. flushUntil defined in 15 files confirmed. matchMedia appears in 39 files and the literal '(max-width: 899px)' 93 times by my grep (higher than reported); useIsMobile.ts:3 MOBILE_QUERY is not exported; shared mobileViewport used by 11 files, installMobileViewport redefined in 7. Plan is sound; the ResizeObserver no-op in testSetup.ts is reasonable but verify tests that assert on observe calls (StubResizeObserver users) are unaffected.
revised_fix_plan: Same as original, but swap local deferred only where the local copy is a subset of the shared API, export MOBILE_QUERY, and add the ResizeObserver no-op as an opt-out default only after checking the 11 StubResizeObserver users.

title: 58 test files hand-roll CSS parsing although styles/cssBlock.ts exists
note: Verified: comment-strip regex present in 59 files; 11 files import cssBlock; cssBlock.ts has readModuleCss, blockBody, topRuleBlock (first top-level rule, column-0 anchored), mediaBlock but no comment stripping. Local parsers pick rules differently, so semantic drift is real. Important: docs/developing-evener/testing.md:1635-1641 itself recommends the inline readFileSync(...).replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, '') snippet, so the docs must change with the helper (evergreen docs rule). The 'tests that merely restate a declaration' sub-claim is a judgment call and already presented as a question to Jesse; leave as such.
revised_fix_plan: Make readModuleCss strip comments (unit test in cssBlock.test.ts), update the testing.md section at ~1635 to point to it, migrate callers file by file, delete local parsers; keep rule-selection semantics per caller via explicit first/last option.

title: Copy is still the test oracle in thousands of assertions; the ratchet only catches tests named like 'shows X'
note: Violation is real and the cited examples check out: StatusBar.test.tsx:414 toBe('Waiting on 3 subagents'); LivenessLine.test.tsx:134 'Waiting on 1 subagent'; NotificationCard.test.tsx:247 toContain('Delegate completed'); WarningItem.test.tsx:189 toContain('Output allocation reduced for inst/model: requested=100 admitted=50'). Counts re-measured: getBy/queryBy/findByText("literal") ~1,921, textContent toBe("literal") 681. These are upper bounds (fixture round-trips are allowed per testing.md). Audit allowlist has 10 rows, confirmed. The proposed new 'second-tier ratchet' is a new mechanism; given Jesse's simplicity-over-mechanism stance and the existing copyonly audit, prefer converting the densest files opportunistically (and when touching files for findings 3-8) rather than building a second audit tier unless Jesse asks. Any production data-* hook additions need Jesse's approval (widget-prop rule).
revised_fix_plan: Convert densest files (Spawn, Composer, AppShell, CredentialsSection, RailRow) to behavior/role/data-testid assertions in separate PRs; ask Jesse before building a second ratchet tier. Treat counts as upper bounds and triage fixture round-trips out first.

title: Browser-guard entries are monoliths with duplicated scaffolding (overflowharness-entry is 2,018 lines)
note: Sizes verified: overflowharness-entry 2,018, shellguard 1,043, transcriptscrollguard 871, spawnguard 767. window.* exports at 2007-2018 (about 10 plus composerRequests); 13 'kata xxxx' references in dev/. Duplicated scaffolding is real but these files only run on Chrome hosts/CI via make test-web-browser, are not on the vitest critical path, and the proposed split cannot be locally verified (no running suites allowed/needed). The extraction of a guardKit is worth doing only with finding 4's shared fixtures; the standalone mode-split of overflowharness-entry is cosmetic and risky without a Chrome run. Downgrade to low.
revised_fix_plan: Fold into finding 4: have the guard entries import the shared Thread/capabilities fixtures. Extract dev/guardKit.ts only for the genuinely identical helpers (theme param, nextFrames, waitFor). Skip the by-mode split unless overflowharness-entry is being edited anyway; verify on CI.

Only the history-comment trim and, if desired, the raw-button lint exemption are uncontroversial. Ask Jesse as proposed.
